rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasiyyah began as a verbal noun meaning entrusting or recommending, then came to name the thing bequeathed.
rows.anchor: “Vasiyyet”, lügaten masdar, yani îsâ’ ve tavsiye mânasına bir isimdir. Sonra مُوصَى بِهِ mânasına isim olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Îsâʾ and tavsiye mean asking someone to do something during one’s absence, in life or after death; Turkish calls this ısmarlamak.
rows.anchor: “Îsâ’” ve “tavsiye” lügaten bir kimsenin hayâtı veya memâtı ile gaybûbeti hâlinde diğerlerinden bir şey yapmasını talep eylemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, îsâ with lām means transferring ownership after death; with ilā it means delegating posthumous management of property and children’s affairs.
rows.anchor: Şer‘an îsâ’ لِفُلَاَنٍ gibi لاَم ile veya إِلَى فُلَاَنٍ gibi إِلَى ile isti‘mâline göre iki mânaya gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse uses lām, its wasiyyah means giving another person ownership of property after death.
rows.anchor: Bu âyette ise لاَم ile isti‘mâl edilmiş olduğundan birinci mânayadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr is agreed here to mean property: lexically it is anything beneficial, and Qurʾanic usage can use it specifically for wealth.
rows.anchor: Mal da böyledir. Kur’an’da لِمَآ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether the qualifying wealth includes any amount or only substantial property.
rows.anchor: Ancak burada hayır denilen mal, aza çoğa şâmil ‘ale’l-ıtlâk mal mıdır, yoksa mâl-ı kesîr midir? Bunda ihtilâf edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Zührî
rows.claim: Zührī is cited among those who take the condition to cover wealth without a minimum threshold.
rows.anchor: Zührî’den rivayet olunduğu üzere mutlak diyenler çoktur

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Ali reportedly told a dying freedman with six or seven hundred dirhams that he need not bequeath, since he had no substantial wealth.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali “hayır, Allah teâlâ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا buyurmuştur, senin ise çok malın yoktur” demiştir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report from Ali says four thousand dirhams or less counts as ordinary maintenance funds.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den mervîdir ki “dört bin dirhem ve mâdûnu nafakadır” demiş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly held that a person with eight hundred dirhams need not make a bequest.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretleri “sekiz yüz dirhemde vasiyet yoktur” demiş

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Asked about a woman with four children and three thousand dirhams, Aisha judged the sum insufficient to count as surplus wealth for a bequest.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe radıyallahu ‘anhâ dahi vasiyet etmek isteyen ve çocuğu var, malı da az diye ehli tarafından men‘olunan bir kadın hakkında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı takes these reports as evidence that khayr here means substantial wealth.
rows.anchor: ki bunlar hayrın mâl-ı kesîr mânasına olduğuna delâlet etmektedirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If any possession counted, the condition would add little, since nearly everyone leaves at least food or clothing.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki böyle olmasa idi إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا şartı pek müfîd olmazdı. Zîrâ bir ekmek veya setr-i avret edecek bir bez parçası olsun

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some scholars considered the bequest recommended rather than obligatory because determining wealth and proper allocation requires judgment; Elmalılı rejects that view.
rows.anchor: hayır, mâruf gibi takdîre, re’y ü ictihâda mütevakkıf olan bazı şartlardan dolayı bu vasiyetin vâcib değil mendub olduğuna kāil olanlar dahi bulunmuş ise de doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words kutiba, alaykum, and haqqan each indicate obligation, so the recommended-only view is wrong.
rows.anchor: حَقًّا,عَلَيْكُمْ,كُتِبَ, عَلَيْكُمْ kelimelerinden her biri vücûba dâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse legislated as a religious duty that owners make a suitable financial bequest for parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: mal sâhiplerinin ebeveyn ve akrabînine vech-i ma‘rûf ile sûret-i lâyıkada bir vasiyyet-i mâliye yapması bir farîza-i dîniye olarak teşrî‘kılınmış idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty protects parenthood and kinship, especially the closest ties, from rupture; Elmalılı reads this wisdom from the lām construction.
rows.anchor: vilâdet ve karâbet, daha doğrusu akrebiyet hakkı ve câmi‘a-i karâbetin kuvvet ve derecesine göre halelden vikāyesi olduğu da lâm’ın mânasından anlaşılmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The amount judged proper was initially left to the dying person’s judgment and bequest.
rows.anchor: hakkın mâruf vechile ta‘yîn-i mikdârı vefat edecek kimsenin re’yine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later inheritance verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ fixed these shares, relieving people of deciding them at death and reducing the risk of resentment among relatives.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Nisâ’da gelecek olan mîras âyetleri ile Cenâb-ı Allah bu hakkın mikdarlarını bizzat tâyin etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance law strengthened the kinship and parenthood right, while abrogating bequests to relatives who inherit.
rows.anchor: burada vücûbu müekkeden gösterilen hakk-ı karâbet ve vilâdet daha ziyade takviye edilmiş ve fakat vâris olacak akraba hakkında vasiyet neshedilmiştir

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon, the Prophet said God had given each rights-holder their due and there is no bequest for an heir.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz Haccetü’l-vedâ‘senesindeki hutbesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says this widely transmitted and received hadith has the status of mass transmission and was accepted and acted upon by consensus.
rows.anchor: bu hadîs-i şerîf ümmette meşhur ve müstefîz olduğundan dolayı mütevâtir hükmündedir. Ve ümmet bunu ittifak ile telakkī bi’l-kabul ederek ma‘mûlün-bih tutmuştur

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
rows.claim: The Prophet also said a bequest for an heir is invalid unless the other heirs approve; a group of Companions transmitted this hadith, according to Ahkām al-Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: Vârise vasiyet câiz olmaz meğer ki sâir verese

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore, the bequest to heirs was abrogated either by the inheritance verses’ implication or by the explicit wording of these hadiths.
rows.anchor: vârise vasiyet mîras âyetlerinin işâreti veya bu hadislerin ibaresi ile mensuh olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of commentators and authoritative jurists say the duty is wholly abrogated.
rows.anchor: Ekser-i müfessirîn ve fukahâ-yı mu‘teberîne göre bâkī değildir, nesih umûmîdir

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî, Mesrûk, Tâvûs, Dahhâk, Müslim b. Yesâr, Alâ b. Ziyâd
rows.claim: These early authorities hold that the duty was abrogated for heir relatives but remains for non-heir relatives, a partial rather than total abrogation.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî, Mesrûk, Tâvûs, Dahhâk, Müslim b. Yesâr, Alâ b. Ziyâd hazerâtı buna kāildirler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Two reports from Ibn Abbas place him respectively with the majority and minority positions.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden de biri ekseriyetle, biri ekalliyetle beraber olduğuna dair iki rivayet vardır

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: Dahhak says a person who dies without bequeathing to relatives ends his deeds in sin.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk demiştir ki “akrabasına vasiyet etmeden vefat eden kimse amelini masiyet ile hatm eylemiş

rows.speaker: Tâvus
rows.claim: Tawus says that if someone bequeaths to outsiders while leaving relatives out, the bequest is taken from the outsiders and returned to the relatives.
rows.anchor: Tâvûs dahi “bir kimse akrabasını bırakıp da ecânibe vasiyet ederse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minority’s first proof is that the verse generally obligates a bequest to relatives; inheritance verses, the heir hadith, or consensus remove heirs, but no abrogating proof removes non-heir relatives.
rows.anchor: Bunların iki delîli vardır; evvelâ, bu âyet ‘ale’l-‘umûm akrabaya vasiyetin vücûbuna dâldir. Vâris olan akraba hakkında

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a Muslim with property should not pass two nights without having a written bequest.
rows.anchor: Malı bulunan müslimin vasiyeti yazılmış olarak yanında bulunmadıkça

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minority infers the obligatory bequest must concern relatives, since bequests to outsiders are unanimously not obligatory; they say the Sunnah reinforces the Qurʾanic duty.
rows.anchor: Ecânibe vasiyet vâcib olmadığı mücma‘un ‘aleyh bulunduğundan bu vasiyyet-i vâcibenin ekāribe muhtas olması lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority begins by noting that the inheritance passage also names parents and relatives as recipients of fixed shares.
rows.anchor: Cumhûrun istidlâline gelince, bu da müte‘addiddir. Evvelâ, burada لِلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ buyurulduğu gibi mîras âyetlerinin başında da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority argues 4:7 uses the same parent-and-relative categories and assigns men and women fixed shares from any-sized estate; this fixed inheritance right replaces the bequest duty, so abrogation is total.
rows.anchor: Vâlideyn ve akrabîn unvânı her ikisinde müsâvîdir ve bunların az veya çok terikeden farz birer nasibleri bulunduğu ibtidâ icmâlen gösterilmiş, sâniyen tafsîlen tâyin edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority’s second proof is that inheritance law defines kinship rights and excludes distant relatives, leaving no mandatory bequest duty for nonheirs to survive abrogation.
rows.anchor: vasiyeti îcab eden hakk-ı karâbeti mîras âyetleri tâyin etmiştir. Bununla mîrasta dâhil olmayan uzak akrabanın sâhib-i hak olmadığı da tebeyyün eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reads al-aqrabīn as a relational superlative for the nearest relatives, so distant relatives were not originally included in the bequest duty.
rows.anchor: وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ism-i tafdîli izâfî bir mâna ifade ederek en yakın akrabayı gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority’s third proof says the indefinite wasiyyah in 4:11 cannot be identified with this verse’s specific obligatory bequest.
rows.anchor: bu vasiyet nekre olduğundan dolayı bundan murad burada vâcib olan ٱلْوَصِيَّةُ’tir denemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no bequest is made, the entire estate is the heirs’ lawful right; by implication, other relatives have no entitlement that could make a bequest obligatory.
rows.anchor: şer‘an vasiyet bulunmayabilir ve bir vasiyet bulunmadığı takdirde bütün terike vârislerin hakk-ı meşrû‘u olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Rāzī reports this as analogy, Elmalılı calls it an implication of the text that entails abrogation and says it is the strongest argument.
rows.anchor: bu bir kıyas değil, işâret-i nastır. Ve işâret-i nas dahi neshi ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority’s fourth proof is that the bequest hadith predates the inheritance rules and its obligation was abrogated; a bequest to non-heir kin is at least recommended.
rows.anchor: zikr olunan hadîs-i şerif dahi bu âyet gibi ahkâm-ı mîrastan evvel vârid olmuştur, vücûbu mensuhtur. Ma‘amâfîh bu ihtilâftan şu neticeye vâsıl oluruz

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: Abu Muslim uniquely dissents from the exegetical consensus, holding that the verse’s bequest obligation was not abrogated.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: Abu Muslim’s first interpretation is that the bequest here means God’s inheritance assignment for parents and relatives in 4:11.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abu Muslim says the dying person must ensure parents and relatives receive their full inheritance shares without concealment or reduction.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: He argues that inheritance and a testator’s bequest can coexist as separate gifts, one from God and one from the dying person, so heirs may receive both.
rows.anchor: Mîras ‘atıyye-i ilâhiye, vasiyet de

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: If the rules conflict, Abu Muslim says inheritance law specifies the earlier duty by excluding heirs while leaving non-heir relatives within its scope.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
rows.claim: He includes relatives barred from inheritance by religious difference, slavery, murder, displacement by a nearer heir, or status as distant kin without fixed shares.
rows.anchor: ihtilâf-ı din, rık, katl gibi esbâb-ı mâni‘a dolayısıyla vâris olmayanlar da bulunabilir. Akrabanın dahi ashâb-ı ferâizden oldukları hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion reinforces kinship duties with Qurʾanic commands to maintain family ties and give relatives their due.
rows.anchor: kavl-i kerîmleriyle bunu tekid de etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Abu Muslim’s position in substance defends the minority’s partial abrogation, but calling it specification is wrong because inheritance verses came later, so the ruling was partly abrogated.
rows.anchor: bu zat en nihâyet kısmen neshe kāil olan ekalliyet mezhebini müdafaa etmiş ve fakat buna “nesih” demeyip “tahsis” tâbir eylemiştir. Hâlbuki tahsis târihen mukārin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance’s fixed shares prohibit increase or decrease, so its obligation conflicts with an unrestricted duty to bequeath to an heir; permission with other heirs’ consent does not remove that conflict.
rows.anchor: “nasîb-i mefrûz”, “farîza” buyurulmuş olması ziyade ve noksanı kat‘iyyetle mâni‘olduğundan yalnız vücûb-ı mîras, vücûb-ı vasiyete münâfîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Muslim’s first interpretation gives this verse no meaning beyond inheritance verses; Elmalılı says that neglects rather than preserves the disputed ruling and effectively admits its total abrogation.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin mîras âyetlerinden başka hüküm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı attributes Abu Muslim’s denial of Qurʾanic abrogation to reading 2:106 as limited by context to earlier scriptures and notes some contemporary Egyptian writers follow him.
rows.anchor: siyâk karînesiyle kütüb ü şerâyi‘-i sâlifeye kasr u tahsis ile Kur’an’da hükmü mensuh âyet bulunmadığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted wording of 2:106 is explicit in its scope; context cannot restrict the apparent wording, and denial of Qurʾanic abrogation produces a contradiction.
rows.anchor: مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ nazmı ıtlâkında zâhir, mâ-sîka lehinde nastır ve siyâk-ı nas zâhir-i nassı tahsis ve takyid etmez

rows.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
rows.claim: Cessās reports that some later non-jurists claimed Muhammad’s law contains no abrogation, and that examples instead abrogate earlier prophets’ laws, such as prayer direction.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

rows.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
rows.claim: Cessās says Muslims across generations understood and transmitted many abrogated rulings without doubt, just as they accepted general and specific or clear and ambiguous passages.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

rows.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
rows.claim: Cessās calls the denial outside the received consensus and strained interpretation, while describing its proponent as sound in belief and not acting from bad intent.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

rows.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
rows.claim: Cessās speculates that the dissenter lacked knowledge of jurisprudence, legal method, chronology, and transmitted scholarship, and relied too quickly on personal opinion.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: Cessās invokes the Prophetic warning that one who speaks about the Qurʾan from personal opinion errs even if correct.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i nebevîsinin mazmûnuna mâsadak olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Abu Muslim Isfahani is the only scholar known to deny abrogation in this way.
rows.anchor: evvel ve âhir ulemâ-yı İslâm içinde bu suretle neshi inkâr eden Ebû Müslim İsfahânî’den başka bir kimse yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Abu Muslim’s account, the verse cannot be applied while taking inheritance law into account.
rows.anchor: Bunun re’yine göre de mîrâsı hesâba katmadan yalnız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early Islam may have had no inheritance at all, or inheritance only for children; in either case a bequest was required for parents and other relatives, with children outside al-aqrabīn in the second scenario.
rows.anchor: bidâyet-i İslâm’da bu âyet mûcebince ya mîras hiç yoktu da evlâd da dâhil olduğu hâlde vâlideyn ve akrabaya ber vech-i ma‘rûf bir vasiyet farz kılınmış idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the earlier reports from Ali and Aisha support this account of the original rule.
rows.anchor: Bâlâda Hazret-i Ali ve Hazret-i Âişe’den mervî olan kelâmlar dahi bunu teyid eylemektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is uncertain rather than certain that children and distant non-heir relatives fall within the general meaning of al-aqrabīn.
rows.anchor: evlâd ile gayr-i vâris uzak akrabanın “akrabîn” mefhûm-ı ‘âmmında duhûlleri kat‘î değil, meşkuk veya maznundur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once inheritance was extended beyond children, the definite bequest obligation was abrogated, while kinship rights were further secured.
rows.anchor: Mîras âyetleri mûcebince irsin evlâddan mâ‘adâya da teşmîli ile bu âyette kat‘î olan vücûb-i vasiyyet neshedilmiş ve ma‘amâfîh hakk-ı karâbet daha ziyade tevsik olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the explicit rule making a financial bequest obligatory is wholly abrogated; other implications and indications may still operate under legal method.
rows.anchor: külliyen mensuh olduğu beyan edilen hüküm de yalnız bi-vechin vasiyyet-i mâliyenin vücûbuna ait bulunan ve bi’l-ibâre sâbit olan hükümdür. İşârât ve delâlât-ı sâiresi ile kavâ‘id-i usûliye dairesinde amel edilebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although khayr is explicit in the wording as property, its implications and indications extend to broader meanings.
rows.anchor: خَيْرًا kelimesi bi’l-ibâre مَال ile müfesser olmakla beraber işâret veya delâletiyle daha vâsi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In some cases and for some people, bequests to discharge obligations owed to God or people, including debts and deposits, remain obligatory; this verse also grounds other bequest rulings.
rows.anchor: Dinde hukūk-ı ‘ibâd ve hukūk-ı ilâhiyeye müte‘allik duyûn u emânât ve sâir hukūkun kazâsına müte‘allik bazı vasiyetlerin vâcib olduğu ahvâl ve eşhâs da vardır
